question: In June 2025, the Ministry of Coal achieved a historic milestone with the allocation of its _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**200th coal mine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a landmark achievement for India's energy sector, the **Ministry of Coal** officially reached the milestone of allocating its **200th coal mine** in **June 2025**.
 
• This milestone signifies the success of the **Commercial Coal Mining** auction process, which was designed to open the coal sector to private players and enhance **domestic production**.
 
• The allocation of the **200th mine** is a critical step towards achieving the vision of **Atmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-reliant India) by reducing the country's dependence on **imported coal**.
 
• The **Ministry of Coal** has been aggressively conducting multiple rounds of auctions to ensure a steady supply of fuel for the **thermal power plants** and **industrial sectors** like steel and cement.
 
• The allocation process is aimed at maximizing **revenue for State Governments**, as the entire revenue generated from these commercial auctions flows directly to the respective states where the mines are located.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Commercial Coal Mining Launch**: 
 
 
• The **Government of India** launched the first-ever commercial coal mine auctions in **June 2020**. This ended the **four-decade-long monopoly** of state-owned entities in the coal sector.
 
• Before this, coal mines were primarily allocated for **captive use**, meaning the coal produced could only be used by the specific end-use plant of the company.
 
 
 
• **Legal Framework**: 
 
 
• The auction process is governed by the **Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957** and the **Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015**.
 
• Recent amendments have simplified the process, allowing for **100% Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** under the automatic route for coal mining and sale.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact**: 
 
 
• The operationalization of these **200 coal mines** is expected to generate significant **employment opportunities** in mining-heavy states like **Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, and Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• It contributes to the national goal of reaching **1 billion tonnes** of coal production to support the growing **energy demands** of the Indian economy.
 
 
 
• **Technology and Transparency**: 
 
 
• The **Ministry of Coal** utilizes an **online e-auction platform** to ensure a transparent and fair bidding process.
 
• The **Single Window Clearance System** has been implemented to fast-track the operationalization of mines after they are allocated to successful bidders.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sustainability and Gasification**: Alongside mining, the government is promoting **Coal Gasification** projects with a target of **100 million tonnes** by **2030** to ensure cleaner use of coal resources.
 
• **Import Substitution**: By reaching the **200th mine** allocation, India is positioned to drastically cut down its **import bill**, which previously saw billions of dollars spent on thermal coal imports.
 
• **Ease of Doing Business**: The removal of **end-use restrictions** allows mine owners the flexibility to sell coal in the **open market**, fostering a competitive and efficient energy market.
